# synology_terminal (Resource)

SSH and Telnet terminal-access policy. Manage its listening port, console access and selected SSH cryptographic algorithms here. Omitted flags preserve their current values; destroy leaves DSM settings unchanged.

## Adopt existing settings

Use an initialized project from [Check the NAS connection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elephant-evergreen/synology/latest/docs#check-the-nas-connection). Add this import block with your resource address and the ID of the existing DSM object.

```terraform
import {
  to = synology_terminal.main
  id = "terminal"
}
```

1. Add the resource block with the values DSM currently reports. Use the sample configuration as a starting point.
2. Run `terraform plan -out=adopt.tfplan`. For one import, expect `1 to import, 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`. If the plan proposes changes, match the differing arguments to DSM and save a new plan.
3. Run `terraform apply adopt.tfplan` once the saved plan contains only the import. The next `terraform plan` should report `No changes`.

## Example configuration

```terraform
resource "synology_terminal" "main" {
  ssh_enabled    = false
  telnet_enabled = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `console_forbidden` (Boolean) Disallow console access.
- `ssh_ciphers` (Set of String) Selected SSH cipher names. Omission retains DSM selections.
- `ssh_enabled` (Boolean) Allow SSH terminal connections. SFTP has a separate service policy.
- `ssh_key_exchanges` (Set of String) Selected SSH key-exchange algorithm names.
- `ssh_macs` (Set of String) Selected SSH message-authentication algorithm names.
- `ssh_port` (Number) SSH listening port, from 1 to 65535. Changes can interrupt management access.
- `telnet_enabled` (Boolean) Allow unencrypted Telnet terminal connections.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton identity and import identifier: terminal. Destroy only releases Terraform management; it never resets DSM settings.
